hyperelastic-tube derivation

Conclusion

The CalculiX model inflates the Ogden rubber tube past its pressure maximum. At each of its 40 increments, the pressure of the model is within 0.018 % of the exact pressure of Haughton and Ogden (1979). The tolerance of the checks is 0.2 %.

The exact pressure has its maximum 0.229790 MPa at the inner stretch λ_a = a/A = 2.566. After the maximum, the pressure decreases, and the model follows it to λ_a = 4.0. A pressure load cannot pass the maximum, thus the model moves the inner face and gets the pressure from the reaction forces.

The checks find a wrong rubber model. A Neo-Hooke rubber with the same shear modulus at small strain gives a force 14.2 % too large at λ_a = 2.5. At λ_a = 4.0, the force is 28.8 % too large (see "Wrong models").

The view shows the true shape of the quarter tube at each increment. The inner radius grows from 10 mm to 40 mm. Select an increment:

Made by scripts/validation-reports.py on 2026-10-23, femahoy 0551405.

This case checks the inflation of a thick rubber tube past its pressure maximum (units SI-mm). The rubber is the Ogden model with 3 terms that Ogden fitted to the tests of Treloar. The deformation is large and not uniform: the inner radius grows to 4 times its first value.

Source

R. W. Ogden, "Large deformation isotropic elasticity - on the correlation of theory and experiment for incompressible rubberlike solids", Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 326 (1972) 565-584. Ogden fitted W = Σ μ_p / α_p (λ1^α_p + λ2^α_p + λ3^α_p - 3) to the simple tension, pure shear and equibiaxial tension data of L. R. G. Treloar, Trans. Faraday Soc. 40 (1944) 59-70:

pα_pμ_p (kg/cm²)μ_p (MPa)
11.36.30.617819
25.00.0120.00117680
3-2.0-0.1-0.00980665

The shear modulus at small strain is μ0 = Σ μ_p α_p / 2 = 4.225 kg/cm² = 0.414331 MPa.

D. M. Haughton and R. W. Ogden, "Bifurcation of inflated circular cylinders of elastic material under axial loading - II. Exact theory for thick-walled tubes", J. Mech. Phys. Solids 27 (1979) 489-512, give the pressure of an incompressible thick tube. Z. Guo, S. Wang and Y. Fu, "Localised bulging of an inflated rubber tube with fixed ends" (arXiv:2203.04110, 2022), give the same integral and the same constants (as μ_p / μ0 = 1.491, 0.003 and -0.024).

This is the simplest boundary-value problem with an exact solution for this rubber, a large deformation that is not uniform, and a pressure maximum. The inner face has the stretches (λ, 1/λ, 1): the pure shear of the tests of Treloar.

Reference

The tube is long and its ends do not move (plane strain). A and B are the inner and outer radii before the load, a and b after the load. The rubber is incompressible, thus r² - a² = R² - A². At the radius r, the hoop stretch is λ = r/R, the radial stretch is 1/λ and the axial stretch is 1. With w(λ) = W(λ, 1/λ, 1), the stresses are σ_θ - σ_r = λ w'(λ). The equilibrium dσ_r/dr = (σ_θ - σ_r)/r and dr/r = -dλ / (λ (λ² - 1)) give:

p = ∫ from λ_b to λ_a of w'(λ) / (λ² - 1) dλ, λ_b² - 1 = (A/B)² (λ_a² - 1)

For the Ogden energy, w'(λ) = Σ μ_p (λ^(α_p - 1) - λ^(-α_p - 1)). At λ = 1, the integrand has the finite limit Σ μ_p α_p = 2 μ0. reference.py calculates the integral with Simpson's rule and 4000 intervals. For the Neo-Hooke energy, the same code agrees with the closed form p = μ0 [ln(λ_a/λ_b) + 1/(2 λ_b²) - 1/(2 λ_a²)] to 1e-15.

For A = 10 mm and B = 20 mm, p has a maximum of 0.229790 MPa at λ_a = 2.566. Then p decreases to 0.217814 MPa at λ_a = 4.455, and increases again because of the term with α = 5.

Model

ItemValue
Part1/4 of the tube, 0 <= θ <= 90°, plane strain, 1 mm thick
ElementsCPE8R, 8 through the wall and 16 about the axis, 433 nodes. ccx expands each to a C3D20R element.
Rubber*HYPERELASTIC, OGDEN, N=3. ccx uses W = Σ 2 μ_i / α_i² (λ̄1^α_i + λ̄2^α_i + λ̄3^α_i - 3) + Σ (J - 1)^(2i) / D_i, thus μ_i = μ_p α_p / 2: 0.40158232, 0.002941995 and 0.00980665 MPa.
CompressibilityD1 = 0.0005 MPa⁻¹, thus K = 2 / D1 = 4000 MPa and K / μ0 = 9654. D2 = D3 = 0: ccx then uses (0.1/μ0)² and (0.1/μ0)³ with a warning. Their terms (J - 1)⁴ and (J - 1)⁶ have no effect.
SX, x = 0ux = 0 (symmetry)
SY, y = 0uy = 0 (symmetry)
INNER, r = A*TRANSFORM, TYPE=C about the z axis. The radial displacement is 15 mm in step 1 (λ_a = 2.5) and 30 mm in step 2 (λ_a = 4.0). The hoop displacement is 0.
Steps2 *STATIC steps of 20 increments. *HYPERELASTIC turns on NLGEOM.

A pressure load cannot pass the maximum of p. A *DSLOAD of 0.235 MPa on the inner face stopped with "too many cutbacks" at 0.2269 MPa, 1.3 % below the maximum. ccx has no arc length method. Thus the case moves the inner face, and the pressure comes from the reaction forces.

The node sets F25 and F40 are the nodes of INNER with no node on x = 0. The sum of their x reactions is F. The node on x = 0 is not in the sets, because its x reaction also holds the hoop force of the symmetry plane. Its part of F is very small: with D1 = 0.00005 (K / μ0 = 96540), F is within 0.002 % of the reference. The print requests have GLOBAL=YES. Without it, ccx writes the reactions of the nodes of *TRANSFORM in their cylindrical system, with an L at the end of each row, and fh validate does not read these rows.

Wrong models

Each wrong model has the mesh and D1 of this case:

Modelf_25f_40
Neo-Hooke with C10 = μ0 / 2+14.2 %+28.8 %
Mooney-Rivlin with C10 = 0.18 and C01 = 0.0272 MPa+14.2 %+28.8 %
Ogden with μ_p of the paper as μ_i of ccx+43.8 %+33.9 %

In plane strain, I1 = I2. Thus a Mooney-Rivlin rubber is a Neo-Hooke rubber with μ = 2 (C10 + C01) in this tube. Each wrong energy gives the correct u_outer (+0.004 %), because u_outer checks only the volume.

Tolerance

The tolerance is 0.2 % (rel_tol = 0.002). The reference is exact for the incompressible rubber. The model has K / μ0 = 9654, which gives 0.018 % or less. The mesh gives 0.0002 % or less, and the increments give no error. 0.2 % is 10 times the total. It passes K / μ0 = 1000 (0.17 %), and it rejects K / μ0 = 100, D1 = 0 and each wrong model.

Other elements and a sphere

The same tube as a 3D slice, 2 mm thick, with C3D10 elements from fh mesh and uz = 0 on both faces:

  • Size 2 mm (5 elements through the wall): f_25 -0.90 %. Then step 2 stopped with "too many cutbacks". Neo-Hooke on the same mesh solved both steps.
  • Size 1.3 mm (8 elements through the wall): f_25 +0.05 %, f_40 -0.67 %, u_outer +0.02 %, with 169 iterations. CPE8R needs 82 iterations.

A thick sphere (a balloon) is the other usual inflation case. This case does not use it. The Ogden model of ccx calculates the principal stretches from the eigenvalues of C. When 2 stretches are almost equal, the calculation loses digits. In a sphere, 2 stretches are equal everywhere. An axisymmetric sphere (A = 10 mm, B = 20 mm, 16 x 32 CAX8R, K / μ0 = 1000, 0.3 MPa) stopped in the first increment with "too many cutbacks". The Ogden model with N = 1 and α = 2, which is the Neo-Hooke energy, stopped at 1.3 % of the load. Neo-Hooke solved the step. With 8 x 16 CAX8R, the Ogden model solved the step, and u(A) was 0.003 % from the exact solution. With a first increment of 0.1 in place of 0.05, the 16 x 32 mesh also solved the step. Thus the result of an Ogden sphere in ccx changes with the mesh and the increments. In the tube, the 3 stretches (λ, 1/λ, 1) are different, and each CPE8R mesh solved.

Files

mesh.inp comes from python3 mesh.py. The mesh study uses the options of mesh.py, for example python3 mesh.py --radial 16 --hoop 32. python3 reference.py prints the reference values, the maximum of p and μ0.
